title: Arbitrarily low perfect truncation triangles from an affine finite-free lift
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], U a quasi-compact open subscheme, and F a perfect object of D(O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Suppose K is a bounded-above complex of finite free O_X-modules and its derived restriction is isomorphic to F. There exists an integer N such that for every integer r<=N there are a finite locally free O_U-module M [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], a perfect object P of D(O_X), and a distinguished triangle M[-r] -> P|U -> F -> M[1-r]. The third map is not asserted to vanish.

source.place: Tag 08EG, Lemma 36.13.6, proof through the stupid-truncation triangle, inverse rotated; with M in degree r-1 the quotient is M[1-r]

proof.text: Perfectness gives locally finite Tor dimension by [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor]. Take finitely many Tor-amplitude neighbourhoods covering the quasi-compact U and their minimum lower bound a and maximum upper bound b. Locality of derived tensor cohomology gives a common interval [a,b]. View the supplied finite-free sheaf complex K on X as an A-module complex P for A = Gamma(X,O_X): termwise affine tilde/sections identifies the finite-free terms and their differentials by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. The representation on U is the given hrep. Set N=a-1.

source.place: Tag 08EG, Lemma 36.13.6, proof through the stupid-truncation triangle, inverse rotated; with M in degree r-1 the quotient is M[1-r]

proof.text: For r <= N, we have r<a. Define the module image of P^(r-1) -> P^r, and let M be its associated sheaf restricted to U. Apply [lem-sc-affine-truncation-kernel-finite-locally-free] to the module complex P and the common Tor interval: M is finite locally free and identifies with the kernel of the next differential on U. Since the complex is exact below a, replacing its degrees below r by M in degree r-1 gives a complex Q representing F.

source.place: Tag 08EG, Lemma 36.13.6, proof through the stupid-truncation triangle, inverse rotated; with M in degree r-1 the quotient is M[1-r]

proof.text: Let T be the stupid tail of P in degrees at least r, associated back to X. Bounded-aboveness and the lower cutoff make T bounded finite free, so its derived image is perfect. Degreewise there is a short exact sequence T|U -> Q -> M[1-r]. Apply the distinguished-triangle construction for short exact complexes [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] and inverse-rotate. This gives M[-r] -> T|U -> F -> M[1-r]. The single functor shift isomorphism identifies M[-r] with the single complex in degree r, yielding the asserted morphisms and distinguished triangle. This construction works for every r<=N, without asserting that its third map vanishes.

theorem exists_low_perfect_truncation_triangle
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : U.toScheme.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w}
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    (F : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme) (hF : IsPerfect U.toScheme F)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N < i → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (K.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (hrep : Nonempty
      (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
        Equivalence.functor
          (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
          (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
          (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) ≅ F)) :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ r : ℤ, r ≤ N →
      ∃ M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace),
        M.IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ ∃ P : schemeDerivedCategory X, IsPerfect X P ∧
          ∃ (i : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ r).obj M ⟶
              ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
                Equivalence.functor
                  (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
                  (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
                  (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj P)
            (p : ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
                Equivalence.functor
                  (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
                  (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
                  (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj P ⟶ F)
            (δ : F ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ r).obj M)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
            Triangle.mk i p δ ∈ distTriang (schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme)
